title: Why Beef Prices Outpaced Every Other Meat

segments.label: scene 1 (title)
segments.text: If your weekly grocery run feels noticeably more painful lately, you are definitely not imagining it. The staple of American dinners has quietly turned into a luxury.

segments.label: scene 2 (counter)
segments.text: Back in January 2020, everyday ground beef was still an affordable family standby at just $3.89 a pound.

segments.label: scene 3 (counter)
segments.text: Fast forward to August 2026, and prices soared to an astonishing all-time peak of $6.92 per pound.

segments.label: scene 4 (compare)
segments.text: That marks an eye-watering 74% surge between early 2020 and late 2026, reshaping household budgets across the country.

segments.label: scene 5 (line)
segments.text: Even after edging down just 2% to $6.75 in October 2026, beef remains locked near historic highs.

segments.label: scene 6 (multiline)
segments.text: Other meats faced inflation too, but nothing compares. Since January 2020, chicken breast rose 34% and bacon gained 21%.

segments.label: scene 7 (bars)
segments.text: Ground beef completely decoupled from the rest of the meat aisle. To understand why, we have to look behind the grocery shelf.

segments.label: scene 8 (counter)
segments.text: To understand today's squeeze, we have to look back a full decade. In January 2015, ground beef averaged $4.24 a pound, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

segments.label: scene 9 (line)
segments.text: Over the following years, expanding cattle herds kept supermarket coolers well-stocked, giving shoppers several seasons of welcome price relief at the register.

segments.label: scene 10 (counter)
segments.text: In fact, prices bottomed out at just $3.55 per pound in April 2017, establishing the decade's lowest baseline.

segments.label: scene 11 (statement)
segments.text: Yet that affordability marked a cyclical low rather than a permanent return to cheap grocery bills.

segments.label: scene 12 (compare)
segments.text: From January 2015 through October 2026, ground beef posted a staggering 60% increase, completely transforming everyday household budgets.

segments.label: scene 13 (bars)
segments.text: By contrast, other popular meats grew far more modestly: chicken breast rose 19%, while bacon gained 20% over that exact timeframe.

segments.label: scene 14 (gauge)
segments.text: Instead of drifting back toward historical norms, beef prices stayed pinned near the very ceiling of their ten-year range.

segments.label: scene 15 (statement)
segments.text: The price climb did not happen in a single sudden burst. It arrived through a series of relentless, compounding waves.

segments.label: scene 16 (counter)
segments.text: The first major post-lockdown surge culminated in August 2022, when ground beef climbed 10% over the preceding year to touch $4.94 a pound.

segments.label: scene 17 (line)
segments.text: Instead of retreating toward old baselines, prices built fresh momentum, jumping another 11% over the prior year to reach $5.67 by September 2024.

segments.label: scene 18 (heatmap)
segments.text: Month after month, steady inflationary pressure kept building, refusing to give supermarket shoppers any meaningful breathing room.

segments.label: scene 19 (compare)
segments.text: Every brief plateau simply established an elevated floor, standing at $5.54 in January 2025 before launching into another furious 22% surge.

segments.label: scene 20 (slope)
segments.text: During that same period, chicken edged up just 3% and bacon tumbled 5%, leaving beef entirely in a league of its own.

segments.label: scene 21 (counter)
segments.text: By August 2026, ground beef peaked at $6.92 per pound, cementing its relentless upward climb.

segments.label: scene 22 (statement)
segments.text: The root of beef's surge lies in punishing drought across grazing country. Scorching weather wiped out native pastures and vital water supplies.

segments.label: scene 23 (heatmap)
segments.text: Without cheap grass, ranchers faced crushing feed bills. They had to liquidate breeding cows, drastically shrinking the nation's cattle herd.

segments.label: scene 24 (statement)
segments.text: Here is where biology creates a deep divide. Other livestock bounce back quickly because poultry and pigs reproduce on rapid cycles.

segments.label: scene 25 (counter)
segments.text: Chicken producers rebounded fast. After hitting a peak of $4.75, boneless chicken breast dropped 14% as hatchery production caught up.

segments.label: scene 26 (line)
segments.text: Bacon followed that relief track. After cresting at an all-time $7.61, sliced bacon fell 12% as hog supplies normalized.

segments.label: scene 27 (multiline)
segments.text: Over the past year alone, bacon eased 3.5% and chicken slipped 1.2%. Other meats cooled, but beef stubbornly resisted.

segments.label: scene 28 (line)
segments.text: Cows produce calves slowly, requiring years to grow for market. Until herds rebuild, beef prices remain pinned near the ceiling.

segments.label: scene 29 (multiline)
segments.text: Step across the grocery aisle, and the contrast becomes immediately apparent. While beef surged relentlessly, alternative proteins told an entirely different story.

segments.label: scene 30 (counter)
segments.text: Take boneless chicken breast, the supermarket benchmark. In January 2015, shoppers paid an average of $3.44 per pound.

segments.label: scene 31 (line)
segments.text: As commercial poultry production expanded steadily, chicken prices drifted lower, touching a decade trough of $2.90 in September 2018.

segments.label: scene 32 (compare)
segments.text: Even after post-pandemic inflation rippled across national supply chains, chicken breast settled at $4.10 by October 2026, offering reliable dinner table relief.

segments.label: scene 33 (slope)
segments.text: Pork demonstrated that same underlying supply resilience. Sliced bacon started at $5.59 a pound in January 2015, tracking predictable seasonal supply patterns.

segments.label: scene 34 (compare)
segments.text: While bacon climbed to $7.04 in January 2025, it swiftly cooled off, settling down at $6.69 by October 2026.

segments.label: scene 35 (statement)
segments.text: Because chickens and hogs produce offspring rapidly, livestock producers expanded output in months, keeping grocery shelves stocked and prices anchored.

segments.label: scene 36 (statement)
segments.text: Ultimately, biological reality dictates grocery store economics. Poultry flocks and hog litters bounce back in mere months, but rebuilding cattle herds requires years of patience.

segments.label: scene 37 (line)
segments.text: When drought and extreme weather scorch grazing pastures, the resulting livestock deficit caused ground beef prices to surge 60% since 2015.

segments.label: scene 38 (bars)
segments.text: That deep structural supply bottleneck permanently separated beef from every other protein across modern supermarket aisles.

segments.label: scene 39 (line)
segments.text: Ground beef prices hovered near record territory at $6.75 a pound in October 2026, down just two percent from their peak.

segments.label: scene 40 (slope)
segments.text: Until cattle ranchers can safely restore their depleted pastures and restock breeding cows, beef will continue straining family dinner budgets.

segments.label: scene 41 (gauge)
segments.text: The humble family burger has fundamentally transformed from an everyday budget staple into an expensive household luxury.

segments.label: scene 42 (statement)
segments.text: Have soaring beef prices forced you to switch what you buy at your local supermarket? Tell us in the comments. Subscribe for more data-driven stories.

question: Have soaring beef prices forced you to switch what you buy at your local supermarket?
